_readme: Runtime tuning parameters, shared by the whole pipeline — hence the per-stage sections
below rather than one file per stage. Edit + restart the app; no rebuild needed.
Everything here is OPTIONAL: delete any key, section, or the whole file and the built-in
default from src/tuning_params.h applies instead. Keys starting with '_' are comments.
Unknown keys are NOT silently ignored — they are logged as 'unknown key ... (typo?)' on
startup, so watch the console after editing. Out-of-range values are clamped and logged.
The values below are the shipped defaults, written out in full so you can see the whole
surface at once. Sections: capture, ocrEngine, filter, translation, display, chinese, english.
NOT here: which backend, where it lives, the glossary paths and the startup source
language — those are connection settings and live in config/translation_backend.json.
Nothing is duplicated between the two files.

capture._doc: Screen grab + change/noise gate. Raise the thresholds if a static screen still triggers OCR; lower them if fast subtitle changes get missed.

ocrEngine._doc: Set useCudaExecutionProvider to false to force CPU inference (useful to isolate a CUDA/cuDNN problem). paddleInputHeight must match the model: 48 for PP-OCRv4/v5.

filter._doc: Turns noisy per-frame reads into one stable candidate. Raise the stable-ms / min-frames values if garbage gets dispatched; lower them if subtitles appear too late.

_doc: Generation, sampling and retry behaviour — every knob that shapes the model output.
temperature: 0.0 = greedy; keep <=0.1 for faithful subtitles.
numPredict: max new tokens per line (~64 covers most subtitles).
topK -> topP -> minP are applied in that order. minP 0.05-0.10 suppresses stray Han leaking into Vietnamese.
repeatPenalty/frequencyPenalty/repeatLastN control looping and repeated phrases.
cachePrompt: let the backend reuse the identical rules prefix across calls (llama.cpp); cuts latency.
enableRetryPasses=false drops bad output outright instead of retrying — lower latency, worse quality.
retry* values apply only to the single retry pass, deliberately looser so it can escape a degenerate first output.
lineScoreMin gates candidate selection; raise it to reject weak Vietnamese lines.

display._doc: On-screen duration = clamp(baseMs + charCount * msPerChar, minMs, maxMs), measured on the Vietnamese output. Raise msPerChar if lines vanish before you finish reading.

_doc: Chinese source pipeline. 'Source units' = Han characters.
recOnnxPath/charsetPath MUST be a matched pair — a model with the wrong dict decodes to garbage.
PP-OCRv5: point recOnnxPath at PP-OCRv5_server_rec_infer.onnx AND charsetPath at ppocrv5_dict.txt.
minOcrConfidence: raise toward 0.8 to drop more garbled reads, lower if valid subtitles get dropped.
edgeMinConfidence: trims low-confidence first/last characters (dark margins decode as a stray glyph, typically 嶺). 0 disables.
adaptiveInputWidth false = pad every crop out to inputWidth. true = size the tensor to the text,
which removes the black dead zone the CTC decoder can hallucinate into, and is faster on short lines.
autoCropSubtitleRegion auto-tightens the crop onto detected text. It is a heuristic that CUTS
whatever its size filters reject — on sharp input a whole leading word can vanish. Off = trust the
capture window, which is correct when it is placed tightly around the subtitle.
maxTextLines: 1 = line splitting off. Chinese subtitles are single-line in practice, so the
split would never fire on a real frame and could only misfire on one. Raise to 2-3 only if a
source actually wraps Chinese onto two cards.
English source pipeline. 'Source units' = whitespace-delimited words, NOT characters.
minOcrConfidence here is a STARTING POINT, not measured — tune it with OcrBatchEval en.
edgeMinConfidence is 0 (off) on purpose: the Chinese value exists to cut dark-margin glyphs,
which English does not produce, while narrow legitimate glyphs (t, apostrophe, comma) score low
enough to be trimmed and cost real characters at the ends of the line. Raise only if needed.
inputWidth is 800 vs Chinese 480: an English line runs 3-4x more characters. With
adaptiveInputWidth it is a MAXIMUM, not a fixed pad width. If ONNX Runtime rejects the
input shape, lower it (the export must support dynamic width).
The candidate-length thresholds are in CHARACTERS and are ~3x the Chinese ones for the same reason.
minTranslationWordRatio compares Vietnamese words to English words, so it sits near 1.0 —
unlike Chinese, where it compares Vietnamese words to Han characters.
